description: ADR 0020 (brief 20 Answers 1): the scope of the POC is workers' compensation. A loss-run segment whose printed claim types and line/coverage labels name another line of business is kept, not processed (manifest reason 'line of business: <line>'), listed to the user and indexed for chat, never learned. Workers' comp evidence comes from the glossary (claim.claimType and document.lineOfBusiness value aliases); this file lists the other lines' printed terms. Terms match as whole words, case- and punctuation-insensitive. 'ambiguous' terms name several lines (or none) and are not evidence. Code: LossRun.Ingestion.LineOfBusinessDetector (reads this file; never the other way round).
rowSignalsDescription: Brief 23 §2 (ADR 0020 amendment): signals that classify a claim row, not the document. A row whose claim.lineOfBusiness value or claim-type code names another line is kept, not extracted: it is listed on the period's keptRows with the reason 'line of business: <line> (<evidence>)', counted, and never enters claims or totals; R-10/R-12 tie the claims plus the kept rows to a printed total. Patterns are .NET regexes over the whole printed value (case-insensitive). A code the glossary resolves to a workers' comp claim type is in scope before any pattern is tried.
